headline: French 10-year bond yield rises above 5% amid budget impasse
summary: France's 10-year government bond yield surpassed 5% for the first time in 24 years. The yield spike follows political uncertainty, street protests, and the government's inability to pass a budget.
why: Sovereign bond yields reflect borrowing costs for national governments and serve as benchmark interest rates across eurozone capital markets.

impacts.name: France
impacts.why: Higher borrowing costs increase national debt servicing obligations and tighten fiscal conditions.

why_moved: Bondholders sold French sovereign debt due to political unrest and budget delays, pushing yields to 24-year highs.
